3.1 The diagram below shows simple syntheses of two mononuclear macrocyclic complexes.
Hint: A reducing substance is present in the reaction system.
3.1.1 Give the SMILES structures of A and B.

text_images.description: Heating 4-iodophthalonitrile 'IC1=CC=C(C#N)C(C#N)=C1', 4,5-dibutoxyphthalonitrile 'N#CC1=CC(OCCCC)=C(OCCCC)C=C1C#N', and zinc acetate $\mathrm{Zn(OAc)_2}$ in a 1:3:1 ratio gives A. Reaction of 4-iodophthalonitrile 'IC1=CC=C(C#N)C(C#N)=C1', 4,5-bis(propylsulfonyl)phthalonitrile 'N#CC1=CC(S(=O)(CCC)=O)=C(S(=O)(CCC)=O)C=C1C#N', and nickel chloride $\mathrm{NiCl_2}$ in a 1:3:1 ratio gives B.

subquestions.text_open: 3.2 Further reactions combine A and B into the dinuclear complex E, as shown in the route below. Give the SMILES structures of C, D, and E.

text_images.description: First, 1,4(1,4)-dibenzenacyclohexaphane (SMILES: 'C1(CC2)=CC=C(CCC3=CC=C2C=C3)C=C1') is treated with 2 equivalents of $\mathrm{Br_2}$/$\mathrm{CCl_4}$ and then reacted with tributyl(vinyl)tin (Bu_3SnCH=CH_2) under tetrakis(triphenylphosphine)palladium, Pd(PPh_3)_4, catalysis to give C. Next, C reacts with A in DMF in the presence of triethylamine ($\mathrm{Pd(OAc)_2}$), tetrabutylammonium bromide (TBAB), and palladium acetate ($\mathrm{NEt_3}$) to give D. Finally, D reacts with B under the same $\mathrm{Pd(OAc)_2}$/DMF/$\mathrm{NEt_3}$/TBAB conditions to give E.
